Arrow tables with zuint columns

Source: R/engines.R
zu_arrow_table.Rd

zu_arrow_table() makes an Arrow Table from a data frame whose zuint columns keep their exact types (see zu_to_arrow()), and zu_from_arrow_table() reads a Table or record batch reader back into a data frame with zuint columns. Together they carry zuint vectors through anything arrow writes and reads, such as Parquet files.

Usage

zu_arrow_table(data)

zu_from_arrow_table(table)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

table

An Arrow Table or record batch reader.

Value

zu_arrow_table() returns an Arrow Table; zu_from_arrow_table() a data frame.

Details

They go through nanoarrow rather than arrow's own conversion. arrow 24.0.0 aborts R when it makes an R object for the arrow.opaque extension type that int128 and uint128 use, so arrow::as_arrow_array() and arrow::infer_type() work for int64 and uint64 only, and give an error for the 128-bit types.

Both need the arrow and nanoarrow packages.

Examples

df <- data.frame(id = uint64("18446744073709551614"), big = int128("-1"))
tb <- zu_arrow_table(df)
tb$schema
#> Schema
#> id: uint64
#> big: extension<arrow.opaque[storage_type=fixed_size_binary[16], type_name=hugeint, vendor_name=DuckDB]>

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
arrow::write_parquet(tb, f)
zu_from_arrow_table(arrow::read_parquet(f, as_data_frame = FALSE))
#>                     id big
#> 1 18446744073709551614  -1
